second_order: calling the room to build a Warriors logo
theme_note: These codes all recruit the room into starting a Warriors drawing; they vary from asking where the logo is to giving coordinates, invoking the Trailblazers, and reposting an earlier call.

second_order: helping people find and understand the canvas work
theme_note: These turns make the pixel work usable or intelligible by comparing r/place with a familiar event, asking for or giving coordinates and links, explaining collaborative pixel art, and relating a proposed change or layout to the board.

second_order: arguing whether defending the logo is worth continuing
theme_note: These codes evaluate whether the work deserves attention or can still be sustained; the variation runs from ridicule and questions about why it matters to accounts of being outnumbered, automated undoing, giving up, and defenses of the fun and labor already invested.

second_order: trying to turn the sub toaster-themed for April Fools
theme_note: One local April Fools proposal holds these codes together: setting an upvote condition for a toaster-themed subreddit. Replies vary between urging it on, saying the theme already exists, rejecting it, downvoting, and disputing whether the post earns karma.

second_order: making the effort visible and calling in backup
theme_note: These practices seek more hands by pinning or restickying the thread and by recruiting through game threads, r/nbaplace, the SFGiants thread, or WarOwl's stream. What varies is the venue and whether participants report backup arriving.

second_order: placing, fixing, and handing off the logo tile by tile
theme_note: These codes report the actual small work of building and upkeep: using extra accounts, protecting parts, fixing misplaced or overwritten tiles, marking completion, thanking helpers, handing defense to the next person, and planning cohesive repair.

second_order: naming who or what is damaging the logo
theme_note: These codes diagnose pressure on the drawing by naming rival groups, nearby art, insiders, bots, a void, or poor borders. Their attributions vary in certainty and target; they remain participants' reports, including explanations of opponents and claims about admin action.

second_order: calling people to defend, rebuild, and salvage the logo
theme_note: These passages turn damage or anticipated encroachment into collective calls for defense, restoration, rebuilding, or salvage. They vary from defending 'Warrior ground' and a border to asking for a single tile, a concerted repair, or a last rebuild near closure.

second_order: working out whether and how to enlarge or remake nearby art
theme_note: These codes propose and debate making more Warriors art around the logo: changing LeBron into Curry, adding borders or a toaster, expanding into nearby space, or relocating beside allies. Variation includes enthusiasm, design objections, and attempts to fit additions inside existing work.

second_order: negotiating borders and pulling back from vandalism
theme_note: These exchanges work out how to coexist with nearby drawings: requesting space, accusing either side of crossing a line, honoring compromises, proposing truces, deleting an expansion, and redirecting effort from ruining others toward maintaining the Warriors logo.

second_order: pranking the room with a fake injury setback
theme_note: This single non-canvas April Fools practice begins with a fake BREAKING injury report and includes recognizing the joke, claiming it should no longer work, and admitting that it still fooled or scared readers.

second_order: keeping game-night rituals going beside canvas work
theme_note: These codes capture the ordinary game-thread chants, arena excitement, and toaster-era celebration that continue in the same selected thread as pixel-defense calls; they show coexistence, not that basketball talk caused the canvas work.

second_order: joking about the impossible karma threshold
theme_note: This separate subreddit April Fools exchange questions the two-billion-karma removal rule, explains it as a joke, and asks what ordinary threshold actually applies; it is room conduct but not canvas conduct.

second_order: mourning and making a first account of the final loss
theme_note: These codes follow the closing damage into recognition that placement is over, 'gg' and 'RIP,' regret over the missing final image, and participants' explanations involving monitoring, footprint, targeting, or scripts. They also include the immediate proposal and rejection of a replacement canvas.

second_order: carrying the completed logo into a WhatsApp profile picture
theme_note: This code belongs with no other practice: one participant takes the completed canvas image into everyday fan presentation by making it a WhatsApp profile picture.
